change_log.summary: Added internal temp doneness check (190°F / 88°C) to bake step exit condition
Reduced all sugars ~25% (brown 320→240g, granulated 100→75g, confectioners' 170→128g). Increased cream cheese 113→150g to offset thinner glaze.
Added rolling tips from research, cook log from first bake
Initial recipe from ATK, adapted for stand mixer

cook_log.summary: I did an overnight cold proof with the v1.2.0 reduced-sugar recipe, subbing ~40g water for milk I was short on, and added nutmeg and espresso to the icing. The sweetness level was much better than v1.0, but the rolls may have slightly overproofed — uneven sizing with smaller ones overtaken by neighbors — and I couldn't detect the nutmeg or espresso in the glaze.
notes: **Second bake** — overnight cold proof, short on milk (~40g replaced with water)
Dough was tacky not sticky — hard to form into a ball, left unshaped in fridge overnight
Day 2: waited longer for dough to come to room temp, much easier to shape. Overnight proof removes variance of underworking.
Rolls hard to keep sealed after cutting — tried thread (not great), need dental floss next time
Added **nutmeg + espresso** (2 pinches each, ground) to icing. Frosting tasted good but couldn't discern either spice.
Possible overproof — rolls stuck together, smaller ones overtaken by bigger neighbors
Bouncy/lighter poke test. Possibly slightly undercooked (no internal temp taken).
Sweetness much better than v1.0 — tolerable level. Overall a success.
Made a fresh latte to go with it — coffee pairs well, the bitterness offsets the sweetness.
Herbert went wild when I opened the cling wrap on the proofed dough — never heard him whine like that before.
Prediction: this batch will reheat well — planning to try in the air fryer tomorrow.

next_time.text: Try dental floss for cleaner roll cuts
Try air fryer directly after cooling phase — still warm, might add a nice crust
Get milk in advance — avoid water sub
More cream cheese in glaze — love that cream cheese taste

cook_log.summary: I made the first bake of the ultimate version, using a Pyrex container instead of a foil-sling pan and a blend of AP and bread flour since I was short on AP. The outcome was amazing, but the dough was cold and resistant when rolling — it needs more time at room temp — and uneven rolling caused smaller end pieces.
notes: **First bake** of Ultimate version — outcome was amazing!
Used Pyrex container with lid instead of `33×23cm` baking pan with foil sling
Foil sling: attempted with multiple small sheets — *would have made unmolding difficult*. Pyrex worked better.
Flour: used `278g` AP + `253g` bread flour blend *(was short on AP)*. Worked great.
Yeast: had `5.4g` instant, topped up with `~2g` active dry

step_notes.SHAPE_BALL: Cold overnight ferment works great. Put in fridge after 30 min at room temp. Take out 2 hrs before shaping.
step_notes.ROLL_DOUGH: Dough was still cold and resistant. Let it warm up 30 min more next time before rolling.

rolling_tips_research: Shape before rolling: pat dough into rough square/rectangle before using rolling pin.
Cut an X: cut X on dough ball, roll each quadrant outward, they join into rectangle.
Roll from center diagonally toward corners, not just back-and-forth.
Rotate 90° every few rolls to maintain shape and prevent sticking.
Use guides for even thickness: rulers, dowels, chopsticks alongside dough.
Fix thick spots: lift and scrunch dough to redistribute, then roll toward thin areas.
Let cold dough rest 10-15 min — stiff dough snaps back.
Run hand over surface to feel for hills/valleys.
Keep pressure consistent — uneven pressure = uneven dough.

next_time.text: Use **all AP flour** — no blending. Reduces variables.
Use **single yeast type** — no mixing instant + active dry
Roll dough more evenly into true square — end pieces were smaller due to uneven thickness, not cutting
Try pasta roller for consistent thickness? *Could be fun.*
Pyrex with foil lining works great — could skip foil but makes cleanup easier

cook_log.summary: Experimental bake — tried tangzhong (20g bread flour + 100g water), bread flour for main dough, and cupcake tin instead of Pyrex. Bottoms and centers stuck, gelatinized sugar was hard to eat. Not great overall.
notes: Tried tangzhong: 20g bread flour + 100g water. Used bread flour for main dough.
Lightweight mixing, treated like autolyse — let dough rest, then slap and folds, reshaped to ball.
Used cupcake tin instead of glass Pyrex pan.
Bottoms and centers of rolls stuck to cupcake tin. Gelatinized sugar hardened — hard to eat.
Didn't love bread flour for this recipe. Not great overall.

next_time.text: Go back to AP flour and Pyrex — don't fix what ain't broken
If revisiting tangzhong, try with AP flour and Pyrex to isolate the variable

photos.alt: Both baking vessels in the oven — cupcake tin with individual buns on left, Pyrex glass dish with clustered buns on right. Pre-bake or early bake stage, dough still pale and rising.

Overhead view of baked cinnamon buns in Pyrex glass dish. Golden-brown tops with caramelized edges, buns touching and risen together. These are the Pyrex batch that released cleanly compared to the cupcake tin.
Baked cinnamon buns transferred to a white box lined with parchment paper. Buns are golden-brown on top with visible cinnamon swirl layers. Arranged loosely after removal from baking vessels.

Cupcake tin aftermath — buns stuck to cups with gelatinized sugar residue visible in each well. Tongs gripping one bun mid-extraction. Shows the sticking problem from baking in individual cups without adequate greasing.

bake_notes.raw: i am trying 20g bread flour thangzhong 100 water. tried to vary the bread flour but needed to add a little more. right now i'm still working the dough and checking back on it. i mixed it a while ago. like an hour. but keeping an eye on it. did a very lightweight mixing and treated it kinda like autolyse where i let the dough rest. did some slap and folds and reshaped to a ball and it's sitting on counter now

use bread flour this time. gotta say i dont love it. also experimented with the cupcake tin instead of using the glass pan. really shouldn't fix what ain't broken. will make sure to get a successful bake of this later this week

vessels.name: Stand Mixer Bowl
vessels.reuse: Dry mix → dough → first rise → freed after punch

states.title: Create Warm Environment
states.direction: Heat oven to 200°F (95°C), then turn OFF. This creates a warm proofing environment.
states.exit_condition: Oven reached temperature and is now OFF

states.title: Make Foil Sling
states.direction: Line 33×23cm pan with a foil sling. Grease foil thoroughly.
states.exit_condition: Foil sling in pan with overhanging handles, greased

notes.text: Foil sling = two perpendicular sheets with overhang for lifting

states.title: Bloom Yeast
states.direction: In liquid measure, heat 177g milk to 110°F (43°C). Whisk in yeast until dissolved. Whisk in eggs.
states.exit_condition: Yeast dissolved, eggs incorporated, mixture homogeneous

notes.text: Milk must be 105-115°F (40-46°C). Too hot kills yeast.
Store leftover yeast in airtight container in freezer — lasts 6+ months. No need to thaw before use.

states.title: Combine Dry in Mixer
states.direction: In stand mixer bowl, combine flour, cornstarch, granulated sugar, and 9g salt. Whisk briefly by hand to distribute.
states.exit_condition: Dry ingredients evenly combined in mixer bowl

notes.text: Cornstarch is the secret to extra-tender texture

states.title: Add Wet to Dry
states.direction: Attach dough hook. With mixer on LOW, slowly stream in yeast-milk-egg mixture. Mix until dough comes together.
states.exit_condition: Shaggy dough formed, no dry flour visible

states.title: Incorporate Butter
states.direction: Increase to MEDIUM speed. Add 170g softened butter ONE TABLESPOON AT A TIME, waiting for each to incorporate before adding next. Continue mixing until dough is smooth and pulls away from bowl sides.
states.exit_condition: Dough is smooth, elastic, and cleanly pulls from bowl sides

notes.text: If still sticky after 10 min, add flour 1 tbsp at a time (max 30g extra)
Butter must be softened, not melted—cold butter won't incorporate

states.title: Form Dough Ball
states.direction: Transfer dough to lightly floured surface. Knead briefly into smooth ball. Return to mixer bowl (no need to wash). Cover with plastic wrap.
states.exit_condition: Smooth dough ball in covered bowl

states.title: First Rise
states.direction: Place covered bowl in warm oven (turned off). Let rise until doubled in size.
states.exit_condition: Dough has doubled in volume

notes.text: Start filling during last 15 minutes of rise

reminders.prompt: Check dough temperature before placing in oven

states.title: Make Filling
states.direction: In small bowl, combine brown sugar, cinnamon, and 1.5g salt. Mix until uniform.
states.exit_condition: Filling mixture evenly combined

states.title: Roll Dough into Square
states.direction: Punch down risen dough. Pat into rough square shape with hands first. Transfer to lightly floured surface. Roll from center diagonally toward corners. Rotate 90° every few rolls. Target: 46×46 cm square (18×18 inch).
states.exit_condition: Even square with sharp corners, consistent thickness throughout. Run hand over surface to check for hills/valleys.

notes.text: Cold dough? Let rest 10-15 min at room temp — stiff dough snaps back.
Use guides (rulers, dowels) alongside dough for even thickness.
Fix thick spots: lift and scrunch to redistribute, roll toward thin areas.

states.title: Apply Butter and Filling
states.direction: Spread 57g softened butter evenly over dough. Sprinkle filling mixture over butter, pressing lightly to adhere.
states.exit_condition: Butter and filling evenly distributed, filling pressed into butter

states.title: Roll Into Cylinder
states.direction: Starting from edge nearest you, roll dough away into tight cylinder, keeping roll taut by tucking as you go. Pinch seam closed.
states.exit_condition: Tight, even cylinder with sealed seam

notes.text: Keep tension consistent—loose rolls create gaps

states.title: Cut and Arrange
states.direction: Using bench scraper or serrated knife, cut cylinder in half. Cut each half into 4 equal pieces (8 total). Arrange cut-side up in prepared pan. Cover loosely with plastic wrap.
states.exit_condition: 8 buns arranged cut-side up in pan, covered

states.title: Second Rise
states.direction: Let buns rise at room temperature until doubled and touching each other.
states.exit_condition: Buns doubled, puffy, touching each other

notes.text: Start preheating oven 20 minutes before rise ends

states.title: Preheat Oven
states.direction: Remove buns from oven if proofing inside. Heat oven to 350°F (175°C) with rack in middle position. Remove plastic wrap from buns.
states.exit_condition: Oven preheated, plastic removed from buns

states.title: Bake
states.direction: Bake until golden brown and filling is bubbling, rotating pan halfway through.
states.exit_condition: Deep golden brown, filling visibly melted and bubbling. Internal temp 190°F (88°C).

notes.text: Check at 35 min—ovens vary. Target is golden, not pale.

states.title: Cool
states.direction: Transfer pan to wire rack. Let cool.
states.exit_condition: Buns warm but not molten-hot

notes.text: Filling is extremely hot—wait the full time

states.title: Make Glaze
states.direction: In small bowl (V2, now empty), whisk cream cheese, 15g milk, vanilla, and confectioners' sugar until smooth. Add pinch of salt.
states.exit_condition: Smooth, spreadable glaze with no lumps

notes.text: Make during COOL step to save time

states.title: First Glaze Application
states.direction: Spread HALF the glaze evenly over warm buns while still in pan.
states.exit_condition: First layer of glaze applied

states.title: Unmold Buns
states.direction: Grip the foil sling handles on opposite sides. Lift straight up and transfer buns to serving platter or cutting board. Peel back foil edges.
states.exit_condition: Buns transferred to serving surface, foil peeled back

states.title: Final Glaze
states.direction: Spread remaining glaze over top. Serve warm.
states.exit_condition: Buns fully glazed and ready to serve

methods.detail: 300°F (150°C), 5 min. Loosely wrap in foil — cover top if dried out.
Room temp, covered. Best within 2 days.
